1) Can you outline a simple pilot packaging option for the next 6 weeks (TPU/GPU mix, token commitments, and what counts against credits)?
2) We run a high ratio of short chat requests with intermittent long-document summarization. How should we think about batching vs KV-prefix caching and the recommended quantization level to hit the unit-cost target?

Attached is a very rough weekly usage estimate. Also, procurement wants to see any standard concession playbook you use for six-week pilots.

Appreciate a short checklist we can share internally.

Subject: Re: Pilot packaging & performance questions

Claire — thanks, this is perfect context. Short answers first, then a recommended pilot construct: 

- Pilot packaging: We typically offer a 6-week pilot with a reserved GPU pool (dedicated slice) sized for peak concurrency plus a small hosted fallback band. For six weeks we can provide a pilot credit tranche that covers steady-state tokens + 20% buffer on spikes. We carve commits into: baseline tokens (billed against credits) and overage (metered).

- Batching vs caching: For chat-heavy workloads with repeated prefixes, KV-prefix caching gives the best latency/cost win for low-latency flows. Use batching for bursts of asynchronous summarization where 50–200 ms extra queuing is tolerable. We can tune the continuous-batcher window to prioritize latency-critical paths and route longer jobs to a cached/batched queue.

- Quantization: For your summarization model, 4-bit quant (q4) tends to preserve quality while cutting memory and cost substantially. For chat LLMs we recommend mixed quant profiles — q4 for encoder-heavy layers and q8 for final layers for safety. We can run a quick eval on your dev prompt set during week 0 to confirm accuracy tradeoffs.

Recommended 6-week pilot (high level):
1) Week 0: Baseline eval — run ~500 representative prompts across chat + summarization, validate q4/q8 profile.
2) Week 1–2: Provision dedicated pool for chat traffic (sized for p95 concurrency), enable KV-prefix caching for top 200 prefixes.
3) Week 3–4: Route batch summarization jobs to autoscaled batched workers; enable aggressive batching windows for low-cost runs.
4) Week 5–6: Stress test, collect token-level cost breakdown, and finalize commit proposal.

Concessions: For pilot we typically provide up to 20% in pooled credits and a one-time implementation credit to cover integration work. If procurement needs a larger credit they’ll need to align on a short-term commit.

I’ve looped in Monica for packaging/pricing details and Connor for the contract path. I’ll also upload a one-page SOW draft and a sample mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Vivek

Claire — a few tactical notes from packaging/ops side and a small commercial sketch: 

Operational suggestions
- Dedicated slice sizing: use p95 concurrency from your spreadsheet and add 30% headroom; we can size a 2-GPU slice (A10G-equivalent) for moderate concurrency or a 4-GPU slice if you need SOC-2 background processing on the same pool.
- Caching scope: start with top 200 prefixes (as Vivek suggested). We’ll instrument cache hit metrics and expand prefixes if hit rate > 60% within two weeks.
- Batching: set batch windows for summarization at 75–125 ms initially; can be relaxed to 250 ms for nightly bulk runs.

Quantization & quality guardrails
- Run a 500-prompt A/B using q4 vs q8 on your summarization prompts. If ROUGE/QA deltas are <2% we recommend proceeding with q4 for cost savings. For chat, keep response-critical paths at q8 if you have tight hallucination tolerances.

Commercial sketch (pilot)
- 6-week pilot: 100k baseline tokens/week included in credits + 20% buffer (credits cover baseline + buffer).
- Implementation credit: $6k implementation credit (one-time) to cover integration + eval tooling.
- If Finlytics signs a 12-month committed band within 30 days of pilot completion, we’ll apply a one-time 10% credit on the first quarter’s overage bill as a close incentive.

Questions/asks for procurement
- Confirm whether the included 100k baseline tokens/week matches the attached estimate (we can re-slice).
- Do you require SOC-2 attestation before the pilot? If yes, we’ll prioritize the private VPC plane (adds ~10 business days).

I attached a short pilot MOU (SOW) and a usage workbook populated with our baseline assumptions. I’ll be available for a 30-min procurement walk-through tomorrow at 10:00 PT if that helps.

Best,
Monica Patel
